chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام used to perform two rakʿahs every night on behalf of his child, and two rakʿahs every night on behalf of his parents. I said to him, “May I be your ransom, how did the night come to be for the child?” He said, “Because the bed is for the child.”
He said: and he used to recite in those two: “Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of Decree” and “Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar.”
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام recite in the two rakʿahs he prayed on behalf of his child and parents?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام would offer voluntary salat (prayer) on behalf of his child and his parents, assigning the night prayer to the child and explaining it by saying that the bed belongs to the child. It also records the surahs he would recite in those rakʿahs, showing a devotional practice connected with family members and gifted acts of worship.
